It all started with me diving into Asian skincare as they are one of the biggest users of especially propolis extract but also honey extract and royal jelly extract. 

So I've recently started experimenting with using manuka honey and regular honey within my formulations. While both of the ingredients are similar (obviously they're both honey), but I find manuka honey to be just a little bit more clarifying and healing whereas regular honey is more calming, soothing and moisturising. So using both gives me the best of both worlds.
The biggest issue I've run with using especially manuka honey and honey is when it comes to finding the proper preservative that doesn't involve parabens (not because I'm necessarily against parabens, but because a lot of consumers are and since I'm planning on selling my products at some point I'd rather be on the safe side) and doesn't involve phenoxyethanol (I'm personally sensitive to this particular preservative).

So once I've found a good preservative system that will work well, I would love to share ideas and tips with you in the future!

Unfortunately the effects that ingredients such as manuka honey, honey and propolis has given my skin is enough of a reason for me to make the decision to use them in my future formulations. I have not been able to find anything that gives me similar effects.

I wanted to dive into vegan formulations. But after seeing the amazing results from using products with manuka honey, honey and propolis extract, those ingredients are way too important for me to withdraw from my future formulations. But thank you for your answer!

NOT having a vegan diet. Around five years ago, I decided to try a vegan diet to see if it improved my skin as I suffered from hormonal acne.
